items.title: The plant hospital in your pocket
items.body:
Your fiddle-leaf fig can't tell you it's drowning. Sprout can.

Snap a photo, get a diagnosis in seconds — and if it's serious, the treatment shows up at your door before the leaves start dropping.

Something is sprouting next week.
items.purpose: Advisory directive #1: open on the diagnosis moment, not the subscription — the deep swarm trusted the product only after seeing it work on a sick plant.
items.callToAction: Follow for launch week — early birds get their first rescue kit free.
items.imagePrompt: Close-up of a hand holding a phone over a wilting fiddle-leaf fig, the screen showing a soft green diagnostic overlay tracing a browning leaf; warm apartment morning light, shallow depth of field, hopeful mood, no text overlays

items.title: POV: your monstera files a complaint
items.body:
POV: you watered it. You misted it. You played it Mozart.

It's still dying, and it will not tell you why.

Next week, it starts talking. Kind of.
items.purpose: Advisory directive #3: humor carried the race on short-form video — the sim's Gen-Z cohort shared the self-deprecating angle 2.4x more than the earnest one.
items.callToAction: Follow so you're there when it starts talking.
items.imagePrompt: A dramatic monstera deliciosa on a stool under a single moody spotlight like a talk-show guest, one leaf raised as if mid-argument; deep green tones, playful theatrical lighting, no text overlays

items.title: Roast our plant-rescue app before we launch it
items.body:
We're two people who built an app that mails your plant medicine before you know it's sick. $6/month, cancel whenever.

r/houseplants, do your worst: what would make you never install this? Top roast gets a year free (and we'll fix what you flag).
items.purpose: Objection ledger, entry 2: the swarm's biggest blocker was subscription distrust. Inviting the roast pre-launch converts the most skeptical cohort into the credibility test.
items.callToAction: Comment your dealbreaker — top roast gets a year free.
items.imagePrompt: Flat-lay of a small cardboard rescue kit box open on a wooden table: soil pouch, tiny amber treatment bottle, copper plant tools, one yellowing pothos leaf beside it; honest documentary style, natural light, no text overlays

items.title: Tomorrow: your plants get a doctor
items.body:
A year ago my rubber plant died while I was on vacation. The internet said overwatering. It was root rot.

So we built Sprout: photo diagnosis that actually works, smart reminders that adapt to your light and seasons, and a rescue kit that ships itself when a plant is in trouble.

Live on the App Store tomorrow. $6/month. First diagnosis free, no card.
items.purpose: Advisory directive #2: founder-led storytelling scored highest with the trust-sensitive cohorts — the panel required the origin story before any pricing mention.
items.callToAction: Set a reminder — link drops 9am ET tomorrow.
items.imagePrompt: A rubber plant silhouetted on a windowsill at dusk, one healthy new leaf unfurling and catching the last light; quiet, cinematic, slightly nostalgic mood, muted warm tones, no text overlays

items.title: Sprout is live — save the plant you were about to give up on
items.body:
Slide 1: It's alive. (So is your calathea, probably.)
Slide 2: Photo → diagnosis in 10 seconds. 340 conditions, trained on real horticulturist calls.
Slide 3: Reminders that know your window faces north.
Slide 4: The rescue kit: when Sprout spots trouble, the fix ships automatically.
Slide 5: $6/month. First diagnosis free. Your first save is on us.
items.purpose: The launch-day anchor: the winning strategy's core promise ('rescue, not guilt') compressed into the carousel format the sim's highest-reach cohort actually finishes.
items.callToAction: Download Sprout — first diagnosis free, link in bio.
items.imagePrompt: A lush, thriving apartment jungle shelf — calathea, pothos, snake plant — with one phone propped among the pots showing a subtle green check mark glow on its screen; bright editorial style, fresh greens, celebratory but calm, no text overlays

items.title: We're live — and your first rescue is free
items.body:
You joined the waitlist because a plant you loved was struggling.

Sprout is on the App Store now. Your early-access code inside unlocks the founding rate — $4/month for your first year — plus a free rescue kit on your first flagged diagnosis.

Code expires in 72 hours. Your calathea has less patience than that.
items.purpose: Objection ledger, entry 1: price sensitivity peaked at $6 — the panel's counter was a founding rate for the warmest audience, converting urgency without discounting publicly.
items.callToAction: Redeem your founding rate — 72 hours only.
items.imagePrompt: Overhead shot of a welcome package: small rescue kit box with a sprout-green ribbon, a plant tag card, phone beside it on pale linen; soft studio light, generous negative space, warm and giftable feel, no text overlays

items.title: Unboxing the kit your app ordered for you
items.body:
Day 3 of Sprout being live: someone's app detected spider mites on a Tuesday and the treatment arrived Thursday.

Here's what's inside a rescue kit — and how the app knew before she did.
items.purpose: Advisory directive #4: proof-of-magic content sustains the launch spike — the sim showed reach collapsing by D+4 without a concrete 'it actually worked' artifact.
items.callToAction: Duet this with your sickest plant — best case gets a free kit.
items.imagePrompt: Hands opening a compact kraft rescue kit on a kitchen counter, neem oil bottle and soil scoop emerging, a recovering ivy in the background; upbeat daylight, authentic UGC energy, no text overlays

items.title: One week in: 4,200 plants diagnosed
items.body:
Week one of Sprout, by the numbers:

— 4,200 diagnoses, 61% caught before visible damage
— 312 rescue kits shipped, median 41h to doorstep
— Most-saved plant: the calathea (of course it was)

The landing page now leads with real saves from real shelves. If yours is still on the fence, the first diagnosis costs nothing.
items.purpose: Objection ledger, entry 4: 'photo diagnosis is snake oil' — the panel prescribed publishing week-one accuracy numbers as the social-proof beat for the analytical cohorts.
items.callToAction: Try a free diagnosis — no account needed.
items.imagePrompt: A wall of small polaroid-style photos of houseplants pinned above a desk, each with a tiny green sticker dot, one hand pinning a new photo; documentary style, community-wall feeling, natural light, no text overlays

items.title: How's the fern? (A two-week check-in)
items.body:
Two weeks ago you scanned your first plant. Here's its progress report — and one thing Sprout noticed about your watering rhythm that's worth a look.

If a plant you gifted someone is on Sprout too, you can now follow its recovery. Grandparents love this feature. Genuinely.
items.purpose: The deep swarm's retention finding: day-14 is where reminder fatigue kills plant apps — the check-in reframes the subscription as a relationship, and seeds the gifting loop the panel flagged as the sleeper channel.
items.imagePrompt: A once-droopy Boston fern now full and green on a sunlit side table, a small handwritten-style progress tag leaning against the pot, before-and-after feeling in one frame; gentle morning light, quietly triumphant, no text overlays
